summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for right leg swelling, erythema, and pain that began one week prior. He had been treated for presumed dermatitis without improvement. Evaluation ruled out DVT, and he was diagnosed with cellulitis and stasis dermatitis. He also had signs of pulmonary edema due to decompensated diastolic heart failure, confirmed by chest X-ray and echocardiogram. He was treated with IV vancomycin and ciprofloxacin, later transitioned to oral cephalexin and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. Diuresis with furosemide improved his respiratory status and leg swelling. His anemia remained stable, and he was discharged home with home health services, oral antibiotics, and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms. He was advised to follow up with his primary care physician.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
